youtube.aciklama: The short increment sensitivity index (SISI) was described in 1959 by Jerger and colleagues. Twenty brief 1 decibel increments are added to a steady tone 20 decibels above threshold; the number heard is multiplied by five, so 16 increments make 80 percent. A person with normal hearing does not hear most of these increments, and a score of 70 percent or more is classically linked to a cochlear lesion.
